articles.title: How to Package Shared Python Libraries with pyproject.toml
articles.excerpt: You ship the job. It passes CI. Then, a colleague runs it in a notebook environment, and suddenly your shared utility library throws an ImportError because it pulled in a different version of pandas t…
articles.body: You ship the job. It passes CI. Then, a colleague runs it in a notebook environment, and suddenly your shared utility library throws an ImportError because it pulled in a different version of pandas than the one used in your orchestration layer. Many data teams still manage shared code by appending directory paths to sys.path or bundling messy setup.py scripts that haven't been updated since the mid-2010s. This is a fragile architecture that invites inconsistency. If you want a robust data platform, you should stop treating your internal tooling like an afterthought and start packaging it as a proper Python distribution using pyproject.toml . Why the common approach falls short The "copy-paste-folder" or "sys.path.append" strategy is an engineering debt bomb.

articles.title: SlothLog: one-tap attendance that writes its own slow recap
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady. SlothLog is a tiny attendance app for people who hate attendance apps. You add a name, tap once to check in…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady . What I Built SlothLog is a tiny attendance app for people who hate attendance apps. You add a name, tap once to check in, and tap once to check out. There is no account, no dashboard to configure, and no spreadsheet to keep alive. At the end of the week, an open-weight model reads the log and writes two calm sentences: one warm observation and one small suggestion for being lazier tomorrow. The effort it saves is small but real: no paper sheet, no formulas, no "what time did you get in?" messages. The app remembers so you don't have to. Demo Run it locally in two commands: bun start # open http://localhost:3000 Optional sample data: bun run seed The demo uses gemma4:cloud through Ollama.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 25, 1671: Astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovers Iapetus, Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet. The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan , the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione. When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen.

articles.body: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials.
